content.title: Quaker Street Mural
content.summary: The Quaker Street Mural, created by Denver-based artist Anna Charney in collaboration with the Arvada Arts Culture Commission, spans approximately 2,000 square feet of the Quaker Street underpass along the Ralston Creek Trail. The immersive artwork features vibrant colors and intricate patterns inspired by nature, and it incorporates augmented reality elements to enhance visitor interaction through the Artivive app.
content.body:
![An abstract, painted mural with a light purple base and swirls of artistic blues that look like ocean waves](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=4994)

The Quaker Street Mural is a visionary public art project led by the [Arvada Arts Culture Commission](/488) in collaboration with Denver-based muralist Anna Charney. This immersive mural installation has transformed the Quaker Street underpass along the Ralston Creek Trail into an experiential artwork that celebrates both the architectural features of the tunnel and the natural beauty of the surrounding landscape.

## Location

The mural covers approximately 2,000 square feet of the Quaker Street underpass, [located on the Ralston Creek Trail near Quaker Street and West Woods Circle](https://maps.app.goo.gl/aHVKxkx53JES9CQt8). This section of the mixed-use trail is frequented by pedestrians, cyclists, and equestrians, making the underpass a vital connection point and a prime location for public art.

## About the artist

[Anna Charney](https://www.annacharneyart.com/) is a Colorado-born painter and muralist renowned![Quaker Street Mural artists Anna Charney ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=4995) for her abstract patterns and immersive installations. Charney has built an impressive portfolio of over 120 murals spanning the United States and internationally in Costa Rica, France and the United Kingdom.

Charney’s work draws inspiration from optical art, natural growth patterns, and mathematical sequences like the Fibonacci sequence. Her signature style combines flowing and bending compositions, detailed halftone patterns, and anamorphic illusions to create dynamic, site-specific works that engage viewers with rhythm, depth, and a sense of wonder.

## Mural design concept

Charney’s vision for the Quaker Street Mural turned the underpass into a fully immersive art installation. The design flows seamlessly across the vertical walls and curved ceiling of the underpass, creating a sense of movement and continuity that complements the tunnel’s architecture.

The mural’s gradient transitions from east to west, reflecting the natural journey through the space. The eastern side, adjacent to greenery and Ralston Creek, features vibrant, lush colors, while the western side, opening toward the mountains and iconic Colorado sunsets, shifts to warm, golden hues.

The intricate patterns and forms throughout the mural draw from natural elements such as honeycombs, flowers, shells, and sunsets. These details are inspired by Charney’s fascination with systems in nature and her commitment to creating contemporary works that celebrate their beauty.

## Augmented reality experience

Charney is integrating augmented reality (AR) into the mural. By collaborating with motion graphics artist Jonna Petrou, Charney will add multiple AR animations to densely detailed areas of the mural. Once finished, visitors can experience these animations by using the Artivive app, enhancing their interaction with the artwork and turning the underpass into a cutting-edge, interactive destination.
